ROBOT TUTORIAL — ILLUSTRATION CONVENTIONS

Direction: a calm, approachable racing handbook. Clear geometry comes first.
The original welcome illustration remains the tutorial's characterful cover.

Canvas: 800 units wide, warm white (#fffdfa), self-contained SVG.
Type: Arial/Helvetica/sans-serif. Titles 26, panel titles 20, body 15–16.
Use compact all-caps only for short labels, not explanations.
Panel cards: white, 12-unit corners, #dfe6e7 outline. No heavy shadows.

Ink: #243c4b. Secondary text: #526774.
Car: red coupe, #db5947; dark wheels; pale-blue glass; cream center stripe.
Use the same car definition in each standalone SVG. Its front points along -Y.
The <g id="car"> definition in steering.svg is the canonical copy; copy it
unchanged into new SVGs, then place it with translate/rotate/scale transforms.
Keep the long hood, windshield, narrow cabin and separate wheels recognizable.
Road: #f0f4f4; thin #bbc9cd edges; dashed #a7b9c0 centerline.
Barrier: a distinct hatched strip with a dark inside face, not a road-edge line.
Road direction: blue #397591. Car-heading vector: red #bf4939.
Intended movement: teal #168376. Contact: amber #c47a35.
Force vectors: violet #765897; label them explicitly, not as intended movement.
Always label meanings; colour alone must not carry information.

Arrows: slim open heads, fixed user-space size, rounded line ends.
Keep direction arrows away from car silhouettes, centerlines and labels.
Dimensions: small filled heads, thin witness lines, placed outside the body.
Witness lines may identify an edge; movement arrows must not hide that edge.
Do not put text on top of a measurement line.

Story: one question per panel, one car pose per panel.
Use sequences to show decisions and consequences, not a cloud of overlapping cars.
Keep the road orientation and scale consistent within a recovery sequence.
In side-by-side comparisons, match the road rectangles' size and panel-relative
position. Put measurements below the road rather than shortening one panel.
Distinguish schematic movement arrows from simulated trajectories.
Never imply that a static clearance measurement guarantees a safe swept path.
For a close-up, reuse the same scene through a nested SVG viewBox and label
the enlargement. recovery-corners.svg is the working example; do not invent
a different gap or car shape in the magnified view.

Accessibility: title and description in each SVG; labels plus explanatory prose.
No external fonts, scripts or linked symbol files; assets must work offline.
Check at the actual documentation width, not only at enlarged editing scale.

Integration: keep new SVGs here, reference them from Markdown, and add their
object[data="filename.svg"] selector to illustrations.css for responsive sizing.
The Doxygen IMAGE_PATH already includes this folder. Add the drawing to
preview.html for a quick side-by-side review of the complete illustration set.
Render at full size and at about 600 pixels wide. Check text bounds, labels
against road markings, arrow/body separation, and intrinsic aspect ratios.
Also inspect it inside Doxygen with both navigation panels visible.

Chapter 3 figures are generated by generate_speed_figures.py (Python 3, standard
library only). Edit that generator and regenerate its speed-*.svg outputs.
It copies the canonical car and computes plotted curves from their equations.
Always distinguish model curves from measured simulator data, print parameter
values and axis units, and preserve the same scale for comparison panels.
The side-view coupe is used for vertical forces; do not draw downforce as an
in-plane arrow in a top-down road diagram.

Chapter 4 geometry figures are generated by generate_path_figures.py, which
shares drawing primitives and the canonical car with generate_speed_figures.py.
Run with python3 -B to avoid creating a __pycache__ in the source image folder.
Distinguish centerline arc length from the car-to-target vector, and label
constructed candidate paths separately from any measured simulator traces.

Chapter 5 traffic figures are generated by generate_traffic_figures.py with
python3 -B. Multiple cars are necessary here: label each actor and use a separate
panel for each stage of a manoeuvre, with matching road geometry and scale.
Do not imply that a shaded candidate lane proves the entire driven path is clear.
Distinguish target-offset rate from actual lateral vehicle speed. Predicted gap
plots must state the constant-speed assumption; they are not simulator traces.

Chapter 6 figures are generated by generate_pit_figures.py with python3 -B.
Spline plots are computed from their stated knots and slopes. Label separate
longitudinal/lateral scales in a schematic plan view. Distinguish C1 continuity
from C2 continuity, a capture region from barrier clearance, and zero offset
slope from zero vehicle speed. The seven route milestones can share a knot;
never depict duplicate distances as valid nonzero interpolation intervals.

Appendix A's setup-flow.svg separates physical overrides from copied private
settings. Callback arrows show data ownership, not driving control transitions.

Appendix B's texture-lookup.svg and texture-pit-uv.svg describe resource lookup
and the current side-pit UV mapping. The latter uses the calculated 0.67 image
height boundary. texture-atlas.png previews FAL-licensed checkpoint artwork;
texture-pit-scene.png is an actual simulator crop, not a schematic or race trace.
Keep the artwork/screenshot credits distinct from the new GNU FDL diagrams.

Appendix C's multi-ownership.svg and multi-settings.svg distinguish the red and
teal instances through names and indices as well as colour. Registry slots,
exported indices and race-array positions are different identifiers. Shared
engine observations and pit occupancy do not imply shared controller history.

Formula cards: use the pattern in chapter_3.md. Wrap the opening and closing
div tags in separate Doxygen htmlonly blocks, leaving the TeX formula between
them for normal Doxygen processing. A plain div around multiple paragraphs is
reopened by Doxygen, producing several boxes instead of one card.
Use native \f$ / \f[ equation delimiters so the locally bundled MathJax renderer
can typeset them offline. Give each central formula a short purpose label,
define every symbol and unit nearby, and follow it with an example or decision.
Escape the dot in numbered page titles (e.g. "3\. Choose Your Speed") so the
HTML title is not reinterpreted as an ordered list starting at 1.

License: new teaching diagrams follow the tutorial's GNU FDL 1.2-or-later terms.
